resources.string: A reminder is a notification from Locus; nothing runs when it shows.
A reminder is a notification from Locus; nothing runs when it shows. Without exact timing (Settings → Phone) it can show up to 10 minutes late.
Locus needs to read your calendar to see entries coming up.
Words in the title, place or notes, e.g. “standup”. Empty for every entry.
Not the topic task results go to. A long, random name keeps others from posting to it.
Kept in Locus’s encrypted vault and sent only to this server.
Part of the sender’s name or address, e.g. “@github.com”.
Package names, separated by commas. Android must say which app sent the event for it to count.
Events in between are skipped and listed in the task’s history. Events found in one check run together, once.
Events in these hours start nothing.
Goes through “%1$s”’s filter as a %2$s. If it matches, the task runs now, even when paused, rate-limited or in quiet hours.
The run reads it as untrusted outside text, like a real event: it can look things up but can’t send, save to memory or open addresses you didn’t name.
What reached “%1$s” and what it did. The latest %2$d events are kept.
Runs before an entry in your phone’s calendar starts. Locus reads the calendar every 15 minutes and plans a run for the right time; Android can hold it back a few minutes while the phone is idle.

Runs when a message arrives on an ntfy topic. Anything that can send a web request can post to one, on ntfy.sh or your own server. Locus checks every 15 minutes, or later while the phone is idle; it keeps no connection open.
Runs when mail arrives in the agent’s own mailbox. Locus looks for new mail every 15 minutes, or later while the phone is idle, reading only the sender and subject.
Runs when another app (Tasker, Automate, a script) sends Locus the event below. It arrives at once; Locus’s automation settings and the list below decide who may send it.
The agent’s mailbox isn’t set up with an IMAP server. Add it in Settings → Integrations → Email.
Every day at 7:00: today’s calendar and what to prepare
Every day at 7:00: unread articles from your Miniflux
It stops listening for events and its history goes. Chats from its earlier runs are kept.
It stops running. Chats from its earlier runs are kept.
Runs on its own, read-only, and notifies you with a short summary.
Current interval: %1$s. Pick one to change it.
First run at %1$s, then once a period. Android may run it a little later while the phone is idle.
The digest also goes to your ntfy topic, so it reaches your other devices.
Waits until the phone is plugged in.
Not on mobile data or another metered network.
Skips the time Android shows its low-battery warning.
